easy.explanation: He says, “In thee, O LORD, do I put my trust.”
easy.q: In whom does the psalmist put his trust?

easy.explanation: The psalmist calls the LORD his “strong rock” and “house of defence.”
easy.q: How is the LORD described as a place of safety?

answers: The net laid secretly for him
easy.explanation: He asks, “Pull me out of the net that they have laid privily for me.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask God to pull him out of?

answers: So he can win a contest
medium.explanation: He asks for guidance “for thy name’s sake.”
medium.q: Why does the psalmist ask God to lead and guide him?

answers: God sees his distress and cares for him
medium.explanation: God has considered his trouble and known his soul in adversity.
medium.q: What does God’s consideration of the psalmist’s trouble show?

answers: My source of power and protection
medium.explanation: The psalmist says, “thou art my strength,” presenting God as his support.
medium.q: What does “my strength” mean in this passage?

answers: Trust, guidance, and rescue from the net
challenge.explanation: He trusts God, asks for guidance, and seeks rescue from the hidden net.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes the psalmist’s requests?

answers: God is seen as a secure place from which deliverance comes
God is viewed as the psalmist’s enemy
The psalmist wants to leave his home
challenge.explanation: The images of a rock, fortress, and defence express safety and protection.
challenge.q: How does the picture of God as a rock and fortress relate to the request for deliverance?

answers: He entrusts his life to God
He trusts only his own strength
challenge.explanation: The statement expresses surrender and confidence in God.
challenge.q: What does “Into thine hand I commit my spirit” reveal about the psalmist?

easy.explanation: He says that his eye, soul, belly, life, years, and strength are afflicted.
easy.q: What does the psalmist describe at the beginning of this section?

easy.explanation: He was a reproach among his enemies and neighbors and a fear to his acquaintances.
easy.q: How do his enemies and neighbors treat him?

answers: A dead man and a broken vessel
easy.explanation: He says, “I am forgotten as a dead man” and “like a broken vessel.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist compare himself to when he feels forgotten?

answers: Slander and plots against his life
medium.explanation: He has heard the slander of many and says that people devised to take away his life.
medium.q: What causes the fear described by the psalmist?

answers: It makes him feel forgotten and rejected
It makes him trust his enemies
medium.explanation: His weakness accompanies grief, reproach, alienation, and the feeling of being forgotten.
medium.q: How does his weakness affect his overall experience?

medium.explanation: A reproach is an expression of shame, blame, or disgrace.
medium.q: What does “reproach” mean in this passage?

answers: He is a reproach among neighbors and a fear to acquaintances
His eye is consumed with grief
His life is spent with grief
challenge.explanation: The references to neighbors and acquaintances show social rejection.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that persecution affects the psalmist’s social relationships?

answers: People flee from him while others plot to take his life
He is standing in a wide place
His neighbors come to help him
challenge.explanation: Social abandonment is combined with direct plans against his life.
challenge.q: What intensifies the sense of danger in these verses?

answers: From bodily and social distress to fear of persecution and plots
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from weakness and disgrace to threats and fear.
challenge.q: What emotional movement occurs in this section?

paragraphs.title: Trust in God and a Plea for Rescue

easy.explanation: He says, “But I trusted in thee, O LORD.”
easy.q: In whom does the psalmist say he trusts?

answers: In the hands of his enemies
In the hands of his neighbors
easy.explanation: He declares, “My times are in thy hand.”
He asks, “Let the lying lips be put to silence.”
easy.q: What does he ask to happen to lying lips?

medium.explanation: He asks God to deliver him from his enemies and those who persecute him.
medium.q: What does the psalmist request after declaring that his times are in God’s hand?

answers: A request for God’s favor and help
A request to hide from light
medium.explanation: The phrase is a plea for God’s gracious favor and saving mercy.
medium.q: What does “Make thy face to shine upon thy servant” mean here?

answers: The periods and circumstances of his life are in God’s care
His enemies are in his hand
His dwelling places are in his hand
medium.explanation: The psalmist entrusts the course and duration of his life to God.
medium.q: What does “My times are in thy hand” mean?

answers: He trusts God while also asking Him for deliverance
He asks the wicked for help
challenge.explanation: Trust and prayer for rescue appear together.
challenge.q: How does the psalmist respond to persecution in this section?

answers: The psalmist calls upon God, while the wicked speak lies proudly
The psalmist is silent, while the wicked pray
The psalmist is rich, while the wicked are poor
challenge.explanation: The psalmist seeks God, whereas the wicked are marked by lying and proud speech.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between the psalmist and the wicked?

answers: Lies and proud speech are part of the attack against the righteous
The psalmist wants to speak less with friends
The passage says nothing about speech
challenge.explanation: The lying lips speak grievous things against the righteous with pride and contempt.
challenge.q: Why is the request to silence lying lips appropriate to the persecution described?

easy.explanation: He exclaims, “Oh how great is thy goodness.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist praise about God?

easy.explanation: His goodness is laid up for “them that fear thee.”
easy.q: For whom has God laid up His goodness?

answers: He heard the voice of his supplications
He sent him to his enemies
easy.explanation: The psalmist acknowledges, “thou heardest the voice of my supplications.”
easy.q: What did God do when the psalmist cried unto Him?

answers: Schemes and the strife of tongues
medium.explanation: God hides them from the pride of man and the strife of tongues.
medium.q: From what does God protect those who trust in Him?

answers: It was mistaken, because God heard him
It was connected with his wealth
medium.explanation: Although he spoke in haste, he later recognized that God heard his supplications.
medium.q: What does the psalmist realize about his thought that he was cut off from God’s sight?

answers: God will shelter and preserve them
medium.explanation: God hides His people in the secret of His presence and keeps them in a pavilion.
medium.q: What does “thou shalt hide them” mean in this context?

answers: Both images describe protection from enemies and harmful speech
Both describe a place of judgment
challenge.explanation: Both images portray God sheltering those who trust Him.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the secret of God’s presence and a pavilion?

answers: The psalmist moves from a despairing thought to recognition that God heard him
His enemies disappeared without God’s help
challenge.explanation: He corrects his hasty conclusion by remembering that God heard his prayer.
challenge.q: What does the movement from “I am cut off” to “thou heardest” show?

answers: The psalmist recognizes God’s kindness and protection despite trouble
He describes a specific military victory
He gives thanks to his enemies
challenge.explanation: He blesses God for showing marvelous kindness and hearing his supplication.
challenge.q: Why is “Blessed be the LORD” fitting at the end of this section?

easy.explanation: He says, “O love the LORD, all ye his saints.”
easy.q: Whom does the psalmist call to love the LORD?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “the LORD preserveth the faithful.”
He commands them, “Be of good courage.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist command those who hope in the LORD to do?

answers: God’s preservation encourages His saints to love Him
The passage says they are unrelated
Only the wicked are called to love God
medium.explanation: The psalm calls the saints to love God while affirming that He preserves the faithful.
medium.q: How are love for the LORD and preservation of the faithful connected?

medium.explanation: The verse says that God “plentifully rewardeth the proud doer.”
medium.q: Whom does the LORD plentifully reward?

answers: He will give inner courage and firmness
He will take your heart away
medium.explanation: The promise encourages believers that God will strengthen them inwardly.
medium.q: What does “he shall strengthen your heart” mean?

answers: He moves from his personal experience to encouragement for all who hope in God
He speaks only about his enemies again
He denies the importance of faith
challenge.explanation: The ending broadens his personal testimony into encouragement for all God’s people.
challenge.q: How does the conclusion turn the psalmist’s experience into a message for everyone?

answers: God preserves the faithful but rewards the proud doer
God preserves the wicked and punishes the faithful
The faithful are proud and the wicked hope
challenge.explanation: The verses contrast God’s preservation of the faithful with His response to pride.
challenge.q: What moral contrast appears in the final verses?

answers: It summarizes confidence in God after distress, persecution, and prayer
It announces a rejection of faith
It describes the power of the enemies
challenge.explanation: After describing trouble and God’s help, the psalm ends by urging those who hope in Him to be strong.
challenge.q: How does “Be of good courage” relate to the whole psalm?
